correctness.rationale: The vertex matrix A=I+S for odd order has B=A^{-1}=1/2 sum_{h=0}^{n-1}(-S)^h. Projecting each barycentric row onto the zero-sum tangent space gives exact Gram diagonal (n^2-1)/(4n) and off-diagonal [(-1)^d n(n-2d)-1]/(4n). Minus normalized Gram gives the interior cosine. There are n unordered facet pairs at every cyclic distance. The odd/even cosine subsequences have opposite signs, strict within-parity order, and mesh 4/n yielding the uniform-cosine limit with O(1/n) Kolmogorov error. Volume and radii are checked by determinant, facet distance and squared-distance averaging. The attached no-dependency rational checker reconstructed BA=I and all 5130 pairwise facet-normal identities over odd orders 3..39, and tested four larger empirical distributions; no finite test is substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim concerns all intrinsic Euclidean ridge angles and a nonconcentrating sine-density distribution for the unsigned edge polytope of an odd cycle. The primary ordinary-edge-polytope literature covers its lattice description, dimension, reflexive lifts and previously known normalized volume. The directed and symmetric edge polytopes use difference rather than sum vectors and are not Euclidean-congruent to the object here. Known general inverse-Gram constructions or an angle spectrum for cycle Laplacian simplices do not explicitly imply this alternating cosine classification or the limiting distribution without the new analysis. Priority remains provisional; exact earlier equivalents remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: The family is natural in graph edge-polytope geometry, yet all odd-cycle examples are combinatorial simplices and their normalized lattice volume is already known. In the canonical unscaled metric, the theorem completely classifies an intricate n-dependent ridge-angle invariant, including exact acute/obtuse multiplicities and extremizers, and establishes an unexpected nonconcentrating sin(theta)/2 law in unbounded dimension. This is a natural complete metric classification with a meaningful asymptotic geometry contrast, not an arbitrary finite slice or routine rescaling. Limitations are explicitly scoped.
